excerpt: Orchata was a Monterrey, Mexico, grocery delivery startup that promised 15-minute delivery from its own dark stores. Backed by Y Combinator, it raised a $4M seed in 2021; Y Combinator now lists it as inactive.
content:
Orchata was a quick-commerce startup in Mexico. Its mobile app let shoppers order groceries and household items and have them delivered in about 15 minutes, with no substitutions and at supermarket prices. To hit that speed it ran its own network of micro-fulfilment centres, often called dark stores, with its own technology for fast picking and delivery. The archived app screenshots show categories such as drinks, fruit and vegetables, beer, bakery, snacks, dairy, cold cuts and frozen food.

TechCrunch reported in August 2021 that Orchata was founded in 2020 by Luis Mario Garcia, who grew up making deliveries for grocery stores in his neighbourhood, and Javier Gonzalez. The company was based in Monterrey, went through Y Combinator in 2020, and announced a $4 million seed round from Y Combinator, JAM Fund, FJ Labs, Venture Friends, Investo and Foundation Capital, plus angel investors. At that point it had been live for about four months and operated in two cities, and the founders described their ambition as building a Gopuff for Latin America. LAVCA covered the same round.

Competition was fierce. Rest of World reported in October 2021 on the race among Mexican startups and giants such as Rappi, Uber, Walmart and Amazon to deliver fastest, noting that ultra-fast delivery had quickly become something every delivery company offered and that Orchata's promise did not set it far apart from rivals.

No longer operating. Y Combinator's company directory now lists Orchata as inactive, and orchata.com no longer serves the app's website. We found no public announcement explaining when or why it stopped. Images on this page are from Orchata's own website as archived in December 2022. This profile draws on published reporting and Y Combinator's directory, and nothing here is paid placement.
